The paper was published in Mathematical Methods in the Applied Sciences, Vol. 15, pages 1-10 in 1992.
The authors are David Colton from the University of Delaware and Andreas Kirsch from Universität Erlangen.
The paper addresses scattering of plane, time-harmonic electromagnetic waves by a perfect conductor.
The set F_A is defined as the span of linear combinations λE_∞(î; d̂; p) + (1-λ)H_∞(î; d̂; [p, î]) for λ ∈ ℂ\{0,1}.
F_A is proven to be dense in L²_t(∂ℝ) for all wave numbers k ≠ 0 with Im k ≥ 0 under specified conditions.
The method overcomes the limitation of Maxwell eigenvalues that plagued previous inverse scattering methods.
The incident electric field is given by E^i(x) = p exp(ikd̂·x) where p is the polarization vector.
The boundary condition for a perfect conductor is [n̂, E] = 0 on ∂D.
Theorem 2.1 establishes existence and uniqueness of solutions to the direct scattering problem.
The reciprocity principle states î·E_∞(î; d̂; p) = p·E_∞(-d̂; -î; q) for appropriate vectors.
The affine hull d_A is characterized in terms of electric Herglotz fields E_h(x) = ∫_{∂ℝ} h(î)exp(-ikî·x)ds(î).
Theorem 2.3 provides a complete characterization of d_A^⊥ in terms of solutions to Maxwell's equations with specific boundary conditions.
The optimization scheme involves constrained optimization with a priori constraints on the unknown functions h and r.
Theorem 3.1 proves that the cost functional has zero as its greatest lower bound, ensuring convergence of the optimization scheme.
The paper assumes the scattering domain D is bounded with C² boundary and connected exterior.
For the inverse problem, the boundary is assumed to be starlike with respect to the origin.
The Silver-Miller radiation condition ensures scattered fields behave as outgoing waves at infinity.
The conditions Im(kλ(1-λ)) < 0 and Im[kλ(1-λ)] < 0 are essential for the uniqueness of solutions.
The paper extends previous two-dimensional scalar results to the full three-dimensional vector-valued case.
The method uses Green's theorem applied in the exterior domain D_e = ℝ³\D.
Jump conditions for surface potentials with L² densities are used in the analysis.
The transmission problem arising in the proof has a unique solution under the specified conditions.
The paper mentions that extension to imperfect conductors or inhomogeneous media leads to unusual boundary value problems that remain unsolved.
The authors reference numerical examples from their 1990 work on scattering by perfectly conducting infinite cylinders.
The far-field patterns E_∞ and H_∞ satisfy orthogonality relations: î·H_∞(î; d̂; p) = î·E_∞(î; d̂; p) = 0.
